cases.name: Kathryn Rose "Katie" Anderson
cases.about:
Her Find a Grave said, "Katie attended Morris Public Schools, graduating on May 30, 2008. While Katie was still in high school, she began working at West Wind Village in Morris as a dietary aid until July of 2008, when she became a CNA and has continued to work at West Wind Village to present. On January 2, 2009, Katie continued her schooling at Le Cordon Bleu in Minneapolis, where she was scheduled to graduate on March 26, 2010 as a Pastry and Baking Chef.

Katie was a member and served on the Board of Directors as a youth representative for the Minnesota Deer Hunter Association for seven years. She loved hunting, especially pheasant, deer and bear. She also enjoyed fishing, cooking, baking and painting. She especially enjoyed the time she spent with family and friends.

Katie was always full of life and you never knew what she was going to do next. She was just as naughty as she was nice and was always able to brighten your day and bring a smile to your face.

On Thursday, December 3, 2009, Katie was tragically taken from our presence, but she will continue to live on in our hearts and in our memories. She will forever be safe in God's arms."
cases.narrative:
He abducted her from her apartment, stabbed her 109 times and left her in highway ditch in Steele County, near Owatonna, MN. 

According to the criminal complaint, Hurd admitted to driving Anderson south of Eagan to a rural area, arguing with her then stabbing her multiple times. Hurd told investigators he left her where he had stabbed her about three miles north of U.S. Highway 14. He said he then drove Anderson's car back to Minneapolis where he bought a bus ticket to Tulsa. Anderson's body was discovered by a passerby in a ditch along 30th Street N.W. in rural Owatonna. An autopsy by the Dakota County Coroner concluded that Anderson died of homicidal injuries. The report stated that Anderson had been stabbed 109 times and died from the stab wounds and exposure.
